definition_en: the most important city of a country, or money used to start and grow a business
core_image: 一切从这里出发的那个「头」
scene: 他坐火车去首都找工作。He took a train to the capital to look for work.
sceneCN: 这里 capital 是「首都」（第 1 个义项：一国的政治中心）；句意是他坐火车去首都找工作。

derivatives.zh: capital 加 -ize 构成，义为「利用；资本化；大写」
capital 加 -ism 构成，义为「资本主义」
capital 加 -ist 构成，义为「资本家」

senses.title: The chief city of a country
senses.definition: the city where a country or region has its government
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或地区政府所在地的城市
senses.example: The capital is crowded with tourists in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天首都挤满了游客。
senses.why: Latin caput means head, so the chief city is the head of the body politic.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 caput 意为「头」，一国的首城自然就是政治身体的「头」。

senses.title: Money used to start or grow a business
senses.definition: money and property used to produce more wealth
senses.definitionCN: 用来产生更多财富的金钱和资产
senses.example: The startup needs more capital to expand.
senses.exampleCN: 这家初创公司需要更多资本来扩张。
senses.why: The head of a sum of money is its main stock, and that stock came to be called capital.
senses.whyCN: 一笔钱的「头」就是它的本金，这份本金后来就被称为 capital。

senses.title: A large letter at the start of a word
senses.definition: the large form of a letter, used at the beginning of names and sentences
senses.definitionCN: 字母的大写形式，用于名字和句子的开头
senses.example: Write your name in capital letters.
senses.exampleCN: 请用大写字母写你的名字。
senses.why: The head letter of a word is written large, so capital came to mean uppercase.
senses.whyCN: 一个词的「头一个字母」写得更大，于是 capital 又有了「大写」的意思。

intro.en: Capital descends from the Latin word for head, and each sense grows from that image of the head.
intro.cn: capital 源自拉丁语中表示「头」的词，每个义项都从「头」这个意象长出来。

items.en: caput meant head, the top of the body and by extension the top of anything.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」，既是身体顶端，也引申为任何事物的顶端。

items.en: capitalis meant of the head or chief, and named what stood first in importance.
items.cn: capitalis 意为「与头有关的、首要的」，指在重要性上排在首位的东西。

items.en: Old French capital carried the senses of chief and of the main sum of money.
items.cn: 古法语 capital 同时带有「首要」与「本金」两重意思。

items.en: English used capital for the chief city and for the head letter of a word.
items.cn: 中古英语用 capital 指首要城市，也指单词的头一个字母。

items.en: The financial sense grew with trade, and capital now means the money behind a business.
items.cn: 随着贸易发展，金融义壮大，今天 capital 指企业背后的本钱。

note.en: Capital shares the Latin head root with captain and chief, and it is easily confused with capitol.
note.cn: capital 与 captain、chief 共享拉丁语「头」这个词根，又容易与 capitol 混淆。

entries.definition: the building where a legislature meets, especially in the United States
entries.definitionCN: 议会大厦，尤指美国国会大厦；与 capital 读音相同，只是拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: an economic system based on private ownership and profit
entries.definitionCN: 以私有制和利润为基础的经济制度，由 capital 加 -ism 构成。

entries.definition: to write with a capital letter, or to turn something into capital
entries.definitionCN: 写成大写，或使资本化，由 capital 加 -ize 构成。

entries.definition: a very large and important city
entries.definitionCN: 大都市，与「首都」同属重要城市的概念。

entries.definition: a sum of money kept for a particular purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为特定目的保存的一笔钱，对应「资本」义。

entries.definition: written in large letters
entries.definitionCN: 大写字母的，正好对应第三个义项。

normalIntro.en: One Latin word for head explains all three senses: the head city, the head sum, the head letter.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「头」一词解释了全部三个义项：头的城市、头的本金、头的字母。

normal.en: cap- comes from Latin caput, head, the same root as captain and chief.
normal.cn: cap- 来自拉丁语 caput（头），与 captain、chief 同根。

normal.en: The capital city is the head of the country.
normal.cn: 首都就是国家的「头」。

normal.en: Capital as money is the head, or main stock, of a business.
normal.cn: 作为钱的 capital 是企业的「头」，也就是本金。

normal.en: A capital letter is the large head letter of a word.
normal.cn: 大写字母就是一个词的「头字母」，写得更大。

normal.en: capitalize covers both of the smaller senses: to uppercase and to turn into capital.
normal.cn: capitalize 覆盖了两个较小的义项：写成大写，以及使资本化。

abstract.en: Picture a body whose head decides where the whole body walks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个身体，头决定整个身体往哪走。

abstract.en: Picture a pile of coins with one big coin sitting on top like a head.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆硬币，最上面压着一枚大硬币，像一颗头。

abstract.en: Picture the first letter of a name standing taller than all the rest.
abstract.cn: 想象名字的第一个字母比其余字母都高出一截。

examples.en: He took a train to the capital to look for work.
examples.cn: 他坐火车去首都找工作。

examples.en: The startup needs more capital to expand.
examples.cn: 这家初创公司需要更多资本来扩张。

examples.en: Write your name in capital letters.
examples.cn: 请用大写字母写你的名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开批头」——开头那个字母要写大，那就是 capital。

root: 拉丁语 caput（头）→ capitalis（与头有关的、首要的）→ 古法语 capital → 英语 capital；同根词有 captain、chief、chapter。

sensesIntro.en: Head as place, head as money, head as letter: three extensions of one bodily image.
sensesIntro.cn: 头作为地方、头作为钱、头作为字母：同一个身体意象的三次延伸。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head, the part that stands at the top and leads the rest.
core.cn: 核心意象：头，位于顶端并带领其余部分的那一块。

branches.en: The political head: the city where the government sits.
branches.cn: 政治上的头：政府所在的城市。

branches.en: The financial head: the main sum that a business builds on.
branches.cn: 财务上的头：企业赖以发展的本金。

branches.en: The written head: the first letter of a word, set larger.
branches.cn: 书写上的头：单词的第一个字母，写得更大。

branches.en: All three senses keep the meaning chief or first in their own field.
branches.cn: 三个义项都保留着「各自领域里居首」的意思。

branches.en: capitalism and capitalist extend the money sense into a whole system.
branches.cn: capitalism 与 capitalist 把金钱义扩展成一整套制度。

intro.en: Capital is built on the root capit-, head, with the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: capital 建立在词根 capit-（头）之上，加上形容词词尾 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and capitalis supply the head root for a whole family of English words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 与 capitalis 为整整一个英语词族提供了「头」这个词根。

items.meaning: chief, or the main city, money, or letter
items.meaningCN: 首要的；首都；资本；大写字母
items.example: The capital grew quickly after the railway arrived.
items.exampleCN: 铁路通到之后，首都发展得很快。

items.example: Several capitals lie on the same river.
items.exampleCN: 好几个首都位于同一条河上。

items.meaning: to write in capitals or turn into capital
items.example: Capitalize the first word of the title.
items.exampleCN: 把标题的第一个词大写。

items.meaning: an economy based on private capital
items.meaningCN: 以私人资本为基础的经济制度
items.example: The book traces the rise of capitalism.
items.exampleCN: 这本书追溯了资本主义的兴起。

items.meaning: a person who owns or invests capital
items.meaningCN: 资本家，拥有或投资资本的人
items.example: The factory was built by a local capitalist.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂由当地一位资本家建造。

items.example: Caput is the source of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: caput 是整个词族的源头。

items.example: Capitalis gave French and English capital.
items.exampleCN: capitalis 演变为法语和英语的 capital。

items.meaning: a main division of a book
items.meaningCN: 书的一章，本义是「小头」，与 caput 同根
items.example: Read the first chapter tonight.

definition_en: the person in charge of a ship, aircraft, team, or group of soldiers
core_image: 站在船头第一个发号施令的人
scene: 船长下令收起船帆。The captain ordered the crew to lower the sails.
sceneCN: 这里 captain 是「船长」（第 1 个义项：负责指挥一艘船的人）；句意是船长下令收起船帆。

derivatives.zh: captain 加 -cy 构成，义为「船长或队长的职位」
captain 加 -ship 构成，义为「领导职位与能力」
captain 加 -less 构成，义为「没有船长的、无人指挥的」

senses.title: The person in charge of a ship
senses.definition: the person who commands a ship or an aircraft
senses.definitionCN: 指挥一艘船或一架飞机的人
senses.example: The captain steered the ship into the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 船长把船开进港。
senses.why: Latin caput, head, gave capitaneus, chief, and the chief of a ship was its captain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 caput（头）派生出 capitaneus（为首者），一艘船上的为首者就是船长。

senses.title: The leader of a team
senses.definition: the leader of a sports team or other group
senses.definitionCN: 运动队或其他团体的领导者
senses.example: She was made captain of the basketball team.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为篮球队队长。
senses.why: The image of the chief on a ship transferred easily to any group that needs a head.
senses.whyCN: 「船上的为首者」这一形象很容易转移到任何需要领头人的团体上。

senses.title: A rank of officer
senses.definition: a middle-ranking officer in an army or air force
senses.definitionCN: 陆军或空军中的中级军官军衔
senses.example: He was promoted to captain after five years.
senses.exampleCN: 五年后他被提升为上尉。
senses.why: Military ranks also name the person at the head of a company of soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 军衔同样取自「一队士兵之首」的意思。

intro.en: Captain comes from the same head word as capital: it names the head of a ship, team, or company of soldiers.
intro.cn: captain 与 capital 同出「头」这个词：它指船、队伍或连队之首。

items.en: caput meant head, the source of the root capit-.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」，是词根 capit- 的来源。

items.en: capitaneus meant chief or leading, formed from caput.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 capitaneus 意为「为首的、首要的」，由 caput 构成。

items.en: capitaine named a military leader or the commander of a ship.
items.cn: 古法语 capitaine 指军事首领或船只指挥官。

items.en: English borrowed it as captain for commanders on land and at sea.
items.cn: 英语借入为 captain，陆上与海上的指挥官都用它。

items.en: The word spread to sports teams and to a fixed military rank.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到运动队，并固定为一个军衔。

note.en: Captain belongs to the Latin head family, and it sits beside other words for leaders.
note.cn: captain 属于拉丁语「头」词族，同时也和别的「领导者」词相邻。

entries.definition: the position or period of being a captain
entries.definitionCN: 船长或队长的职位与任期，由 captain 加 -cy 构成。

entries.definition: chief, or the main city, money, or letter
entries.definitionCN: 首要的；首都；资本；大写字母，与 captain 同出 caput。

entries.definition: the leader of a group or organization
entries.definitionCN: 团体或组织的首领，同样源自拉丁语 caput。

entries.definition: the officer in charge of a military group
entries.definitionCN: 指挥一支军队的军官，与「上尉」义近。

entries.definition: the person who leads a group
entries.definitionCN: 带领一个团体的人，对应「队长」义。

entries.definition: an informal word for the captain of a boat or team
entries.definitionCN: 船长或队长的口语说法。

normalIntro.en: The head root is the key: a captain is the head of a ship, a team, or a company of soldiers.
normalIntro.cn: 关键是「头」这个词根：captain 就是船、队伍或连队的头。

normal.en: captain and capital share the Latin root caput, head.
normal.cn: captain 与 capital 共享拉丁词根 caput（头）。

normal.en: The captain is the head of the ship, which is why the word first meant ship commander.
normal.cn: 船长是船上的头，所以这个词最早指船只指挥官。

normal.en: The same head idea moved to sports, giving team captain.
normal.cn: 同样的「头」的想法移到运动上，就有了 team captain。

normal.en: In the army, a captain is the head of a company of soldiers.
normal.cn: 在军队里，上尉是一个连的头。

normal.en: As a verb, captain means to act as the head of a team.
normal.cn: 作动词时，captain 指担任队伍的头。

abstract.en: Picture a figure standing at the bow, the whole crew watching for a signal.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在船头，全体船员都等着他发信号。

abstract.en: Picture a captain's armband passed from one player to another.
abstract.cn: 想象队长袖标从一名球员传到另一名球员手上。

abstract.en: Picture a line of soldiers turning as one when the leading voice speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一队士兵在领头人开口时齐刷刷转身。

examples.en: The captain ordered the crew to lower the sails.
examples.cn: 船长下令收起船帆。

examples.en: She was made captain of the basketball team.
examples.cn: 她被任命为篮球队队长。

examples.en: He captained the side for three seasons.
examples.cn: 他带领这支球队打了三个赛季。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普顿」——开船的人站在最前面，就是船长。

root: 拉丁语 caput（头）→ 晚期拉丁语 capitaneus（为首者）→ 古法语 capitaine → 英语 captain。

sensesIntro.en: One role, several settings: the head of a ship, a team, or a company of soldiers.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个角色，几种场合：船上的头、队伍的头、连队的头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the person standing at the front, giving orders that others follow.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在最前面、发号施令而众人跟随的人。

branches.en: The maritime sense: the commander of a ship or aircraft.
branches.cn: 航海义：船或飞机的指挥官。

branches.en: The sporting sense: the player who leads the team.
branches.cn: 体育义：带领球队的那名球员。

branches.en: The military sense: an officer rank above lieutenant.
branches.cn: 军衔义：高于中尉的军官等级。

branches.en: All senses name a head who is responsible for the group.
branches.cn: 所有义项都指对团体负责的那个「头」。

branches.en: The verb captain generalizes the role to any team or side.
branches.cn: 动词 captain 把这个角色推广到任何队伍。

intro.en: Captain is formed on the root capit-, head, with the agent ending -ain.
intro.cn: captain 建立在词根 capit-（头）上，加上表示人的词尾 -ain。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and capitaneus explain both captain and its relatives capital and chief.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 与 capitaneus 同时解释了 captain 及其亲属词 capital、chief。

items.meaning: the head of a ship, team, or company
items.example: The captain spoke to the passengers.

items.meaning: more than one captain, or he leads a team
items.meaningCN: captain 的复数，或动词第三人称单数
items.example: Both captains agreed to the rules.
items.exampleCN: 两位队长都同意了规则。

items.example: He captained the club for a decade.
items.exampleCN: 他担任这家俱乐部的队长十年。

items.meaning: the act of leading a team
items.example: She is captaining the side this season.
He took over the captaincy in May.

items.meaning: the role and skill of a captain
items.example: Her captainship steadied the crew.
items.exampleCN: 她的领导让船员稳定下来。

items.example: Caput is the root of the family.

items.meaning: a leader or the most important person
items.meaningCN: 首领；最重要的人，与 captain 同根
items.example: The chief called a meeting.

definition_en: to catch a person or animal, or to take control of a place by force
core_image: 伸手把正在奔跑的东西一把抓住
scene: 警察当天就抓获了那名小偷。The police captured the thief the same day.
sceneCN: 这里 captured 是 capture 的过去式，意为「抓获」（第 1 个义项：把人或动物抓住）；句意是警察当天就抓住了那名小偷。

derivatives.zh: 与 capture 同根，义为「被俘虏的；被关起来的」
captive 加 -ity 构成，义为「囚禁状态」
由同一词根加 -or 构成，义为「捕获者、抓人的人」

senses.title: To catch a person or animal
senses.definition: to take a person or animal prisoner by force
senses.definitionCN: 用武力把人或动物抓住并控制住
senses.example: Soldiers captured three scouts near the river.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵在河边抓获了三名侦察兵。
senses.why: Latin capere means to seize, and capture keeps that physical action of grabbing hold.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 capere 意为「抓住」，capture 保留了抓住东西这一身体动作。

senses.title: To take control of a place
senses.definition: to seize a place or thing by force, especially in war
senses.definitionCN: 尤其指在战争中用武力夺取一个地方或物品
senses.example: The army captured the city after a long siege.
senses.exampleCN: 经过长期围困，军队攻占了这座城市。
senses.why: Taking a city is the same gesture as taking a prisoner, only the object is larger.
senses.whyCN: 攻下一座城与抓住一个人是同一个动作，只是对象变大了。

senses.title: To record or hold attention
senses.definition: to record an image, sound, or feeling, or to hold someone's attention
senses.definitionCN: 把影像、声音或感受记录下来，或牢牢吸引住某人的注意
senses.example: The photograph captures the light of that morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这张照片捕捉到了那个早晨的光。
senses.why: A camera takes hold of a moment the way a hand takes hold of an object.
senses.whyCN: 相机「抓住」一个瞬间，正如手抓住一件物品，于是有了「捕捉影像」的义项。

intro.en: Capture comes straight from the Latin verb for seizing, by way of a noun meaning a taking.
intro.cn: capture 直接来自拉丁语中表示「抓取」的动词，经由一个意为「拿取」的名词进入英语。

items.en: capere meant to take, seize, or hold, and it is the root behind cap- and capt-.
items.cn: capere 意为「拿、抓、控制」，是 cap- 与 capt- 词根的来源。

items.en: captura named a taking or a catch, especially of animals.
items.cn: captura 指「拿取、捕获」，尤其指猎获动物。

items.en: Old French capture kept the legal and military sense of taking a person or place.
items.cn: 古法语 capture 保留了夺取人或地方的法律与军事含义。

items.en: English borrowed capture for the act of taking a prisoner or a town.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 capture，指俘获俘虏或攻占城镇。

items.en: Photography and computing extended it to recording images, sound, and data.
items.cn: 摄影与计算机技术把它的词义扩展到记录影像、声音和数据。

note.en: Capture belongs to the Latin family of seizing, and its near meanings all involve taking hold.
note.cn: capture 属于拉丁语「抓取」词族，近义词都与「抓住」有关。

entries.definition: kept as a prisoner
entries.definitionCN: 被俘虏的、被关押的，与 capture 同根。

entries.definition: a person who captures someone
entries.definitionCN: 捕获者、抓人的人，由同一词根加 -or 构成。

entries.definition: to hold someone's attention completely
entries.definitionCN: 使着迷，字面意思是「把人抓住」。

entries.definition: to take hold of something suddenly and by force
entries.definitionCN: 突然用力抓住某物，最贴近 capture 的动作义。

entries.definition: to take someone into legal custody
entries.definitionCN: 依法逮捕某人，对应「抓获」义。

entries.definition: to take something quickly and roughly
entries.definitionCN: 迅速而粗鲁地抓住，是口语说法。

normalIntro.en: The root capt- means seized, and every sense is a version of taking hold.
normalIntro.cn: 词根 capt- 意为「被抓住」，每个义项都是「抓住」的一种版本。

normal.en: capt- comes from Latin capere, to seize, the same root as captive and captor.
normal.cn: capt- 来自拉丁语 capere（抓取），与 captive、captor 同根。

normal.en: A prisoner is captured, and so is a city: the verb does not change.
normal.cn: 俘虏可以被 capture，城市也可以被 capture，动词本身不变。

normal.en: capture the attention treats attention as something that can be grabbed.
normal.cn: capture the attention 把注意力当成可以抓走的东西。

normal.en: A camera captures a moment, which links photography with the same old verb.
normal.cn: 相机 capture 一个瞬间，把摄影和这个古老动词连在一起。

normal.en: The noun capture is simply the act: the capture of the town.
normal.cn: 名词 capture 就是那个动作本身：攻占该镇。

abstract.en: Picture a hand closing around a bird that was about to fly away.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手合拢，抓住一只正要飞走的鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a flag being pulled down and another raised in its place.
abstract.cn: 想象一面旗被拉下，另一面旗在原地升起。

abstract.en: Picture a camera shutter closing on one second of light.
abstract.cn: 想象相机快门合拢，把一秒的光收进去。

examples.en: The police captured the thief the same day.
examples.cn: 警察当天就抓获了那名小偷。

examples.en: The army captured the city after a long siege.
examples.cn: 经过长期围困，军队攻占了这座城市。

examples.en: The photograph captures the light of that morning.
examples.cn: 这张照片捕捉到了那个早晨的光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开普车」——开车追上去，一把把人抓住。

root: 拉丁语 capere（抓住、夺取）→ captura（捕获）→ 古法语 capture → 英语 capture。

sensesIntro.en: One gesture of seizing runs through all senses, from prisoners to cities to photographs.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「抓住」的动作贯穿全部义项，从俘虏到城市再到照片。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing around something that is trying to get away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢，抓住正想逃走的东西。

branches.en: The personal sense: taking a person or animal prisoner.
branches.cn: 指人的义项：把人或动物抓为俘虏。

branches.en: The territorial sense: taking a city or position by force.
branches.cn: 指地域的义项：用武力攻占城市或阵地。

branches.en: The recording sense: taking an image, sound, or feeling into a device.
branches.cn: 记录义：把影像、声音或感受收进设备里。

branches.en: Both older senses share the idea of force against a resisting object.
branches.cn: 两个较早的义项都共享「以武力对付抵抗者」的意思。

branches.en: The modern sense softens force into attention: a good story captures listeners.
branches.cn: 现代义把「武力」软化为「吸引力」：好故事能抓住听众。

intro.en: Capture is built on the root capt-, seized, with the noun and verb ending -ure.
intro.cn: capture 建立在词根 capt-（被抓住的）上，加上名词兼动词词尾 -ure。

latinIntro.en: Latin capere and captura give English capture, captive, and captor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 capere 与 captura 给英语带来 capture、captive、captor 等词。

items.example: They captured the moment on film.
items.exampleCN: 他们用胶片记录下那个瞬间。

items.meaning: he, she, or it seizes something
items.example: The novel captures village life well.
items.exampleCN: 这部小说很好地捕捉了乡村生活。

items.meaning: seized or recorded in the past
items.example: The rebels captured the radio station.

items.meaning: the act of seizing or recording
items.example: The team is capturing images of the coast.
items.exampleCN: 团队正在拍摄海岸影像。

items.example: The captive birds were later released.
items.exampleCN: 被关的鸟后来被放生了。

items.meaning: the state of being held prisoner
items.example: The animal was born in captivity.
items.exampleCN: 这只动物出生在圈养环境中。

items.example: The captor released the driver unharmed.
items.exampleCN: 劫持者未伤司机便将其释放。

items.example: Capere underlies the whole family.
items.exampleCN: capere 是整个词族的底层词根。

definition_en: a road vehicle with an engine that carries a small number of people
core_image: 四个轮子载着人往前跑的盒子
scene: 他们把行李放进车里就出发了。They put the bags in the car and set off.
sceneCN: 这里 car 是「汽车」（第 1 个义项：在公路上载人的带发动机车辆）；句意是他们把行李放进车里就出发了。

derivatives.zh: car 与 pool 复合，义为「拼车；拼车群体」
car 与 port 复合，义为「简易车库、车棚」
car 与 load 复合，义为「一车之量」

senses.title: A road vehicle for a few people
senses.definition: a road vehicle with an engine, seats for a few people, and four wheels
senses.definitionCN: 带发动机、有几个座位、四个轮子的公路车辆
senses.example: We bought a small car for city driving.
senses.exampleCN: 我们买了一辆适合在城里开的小车。
senses.why: The word first named a wheeled wagon, and the same shape became a motor car.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指带轮的车，同样的形状后来装上发动机，就成了汽车。

senses.title: A separate section of a train
senses.definition: one of the separate passenger or dining sections of a train
senses.definitionCN: 列车上供乘客乘坐或用餐的独立一节
senses.example: The dining car was at the front of the train.
senses.exampleCN: 餐车在列车的前部。
senses.why: A railway carriage is also a wheeled box for people, so English calls it a car.
senses.whyCN: 火车车厢同样是装人的带轮盒子，英语便也用 car 来称呼它。

intro.en: Car is an old Celtic wagon word that was reborn when engines replaced horses.
intro.cn: car 是一个古老的凯尔特语「车」词，在发动机取代马之后重获新生。

items.en: carrus named a two-wheeled wagon used by Celtic peoples.
items.cn: carrus 是凯尔特人使用的双轮马车。

items.en: Latin borrowed carrus for a wheeled transport wagon.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 carrus，指带轮的运输车。

items.en: Old French car named a cart or a wagon of any simple kind.
items.cn: 古法语 car 指各种简易的马车或货车。

items.en: English car first meant a cart, and later a railway carriage.
items.cn: 英语 car 起初指马车，后来也指火车车厢。

items.en: With the motor engine the word shifted to the private road vehicle we know today.
items.cn: 随着发动机出现，这个词转指我们今天熟悉的私人公路车辆。

note.en: Car shares its root with cart and carriage, and it sits beside other names for vehicles.
note.cn: car 与 cart、carriage 同根，同时和别的车辆名称相邻。

entries.definition: a small vehicle with wheels, pushed or pulled by hand or animal
entries.definitionCN: 手推或畜拉的小车，与 car 同出拉丁语 carrus。

entries.definition: an arrangement in which people share a car for journeys
entries.definitionCN: 拼车安排，由 car 与 pool 复合而成。

entries.definition: a shelter with a roof but no full walls for a car
entries.definitionCN: 只有顶没有完整墙的简易车棚。

entries.definition: a car, especially in formal or American usage
entries.definitionCN: 汽车，较正式的美国说法。

entries.definition: any machine used for transport
entries.definitionCN: 任何用于运输的机械工具，是 car 的上位词。

entries.definition: a strong vehicle with four wheels for carrying loads
entries.definitionCN: 四轮载货车，与 car 的古老含义相近。

normalIntro.en: A short word with a long history: from Celtic wagon to motor car.
normalIntro.cn: 一个短词，一段长历史：从凯尔特马车到汽车。

normal.en: car and cart both come from Latin carrus, a wagon.
normal.cn: car 与 cart 都来自拉丁语 carrus（马车）。

normal.en: by car and car park are fixed phrases worth learning as blocks.
normal.cn: by car 与 car park 是值得整块记住的固定搭配。

normal.en: dining car keeps the old railway sense of a carriage.
normal.cn: dining car 保留了「车厢」这个较早的义项。

normal.en: carpool and carport show car combining with other nouns.
normal.cn: carpool 与 carport 展示了 car 与其他名词的复合。

normal.en: The plural cars adds only an s, like most short nouns.
normal.cn: 复数 cars 只加一个 s，和多数短名词一样。

abstract.en: Picture a box on four wheels rolling down a road with people inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个四轮盒子载着人沿路滚过。

abstract.en: Picture a horse cart losing its horse and gaining an engine.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆马车失去马，却装上了发动机。

abstract.en: Picture the car door closing and the world outside starting to slide past.
abstract.cn: 想象车门关上，外面的世界开始向后退去。

examples.en: They put the bags in the car and set off.
examples.cn: 他们把行李放进车里就出发了。

examples.en: We bought a small car for city driving.
examples.cn: 我们买了一辆适合在城里开的小车。

examples.en: The dining car was at the front of the train.
examples.cn: 餐车在列车的前部。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡」——车卡在路口，一动不动。

root: 高卢语 carrus（双轮马车）→ 拉丁语 carrus → 古法语 car → 英语 car。

sensesIntro.en: The same wheeled box serves the road and the railway, so one word covers both.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个带轮盒子既服务于公路也服务于铁路，一个词就够用。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a box on wheels carrying people from one place to another.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个带轮的盒子，把人从一处运到另一处。

branches.en: The road sense: a private vehicle with an engine.
branches.cn: 公路义：带发动机的私人车辆。

branches.en: The rail sense: a single carriage of a train.
branches.cn: 铁路义：列车的一节车厢。

branches.en: Compounds such as car park and car door belong to the road vehicle.
branches.cn: car park、car door 等复合词都属于公路车辆这一义。

branches.en: Both senses keep the original wagon image of a wheeled container.
branches.cn: 两个义项都保留了「带轮容器」这一马车意象。

branches.en: dining car and sleeping car show the railway sense surviving in compounds.
branches.cn: 餐车与卧铺车厢说明铁路义仍活在复合词里。

intro.en: Car is a short base noun of Celtic origin, and it forms many compounds.
intro.cn: car 是源自凯尔特语的简短基础名词，能构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin form carrus, a wagon, links car with cart and carriage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语形式 carrus（马车）把 car 与 cart、carriage 连在一起。

items.meaning: a road vehicle or a railway carriage
items.example: The car is parked outside.
The street was full of cars.

items.meaning: a small vehicle pushed or pulled
items.example: He pushed the cart through the market.

items.meaning: a shared arrangement for driving together
items.example: They joined a carpool to save money.

items.meaning: a roofed shelter for a car
items.example: The carport keeps the snow off the car.

items.meaning: as much as a car can carry
items.example: They brought a carload of wood.

items.meaning: a railway passenger car or a horse-drawn vehicle
items.meaningCN: 火车车厢或马车，与 car 同根
items.example: We sat in the last carriage.
items.exampleCN: 我们坐在最后一节车厢。

items.example: Carrus came into Latin from Gaulish.
items.exampleCN: carrus 是从高卢语进入拉丁语的。

definition_en: a chemical element found in coal, diamonds, and all living things
core_image: 烧成黑色的木炭，仍保留着火的痕迹
scene: 钻石和石墨都由碳构成。Both diamond and graphite are made of carbon.
sceneCN: 这里 carbon 是「碳」（第 1 个义项：一种化学元素）；句意是钻石和石墨这两种外观完全不同的物质都由碳构成。

derivatives.zh: carbon 加 -ate 构成，义为「碳酸盐」
carbon 加 -ic 构成，义为「碳酸的」
carbon 加 -ize 构成，义为「使碳化」

senses.title: The chemical element of coal and diamonds
senses.definition: a chemical element that forms coal, diamonds, and the bodies of living things
senses.definitionCN: 构成煤、钻石和生物体的一种化学元素
senses.example: Carbon is the basic building block of all living things.
senses.exampleCN: 碳是一切生物的基本组成单元。
senses.why: Latin carbo meant charcoal or a glowing coal, the visible form of this element.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 carbo 指木炭或烧红的炭，正是这种元素最直观的形态。

senses.title: Thin paper that copies writing
senses.definition: thin dark paper placed under a sheet so that writing passes through
senses.definitionCN: 垫在纸下、让字迹透过去的深色薄纸
senses.example: The receipt was typed with carbon paper.
senses.exampleCN: 那张收据是用复写纸打出来的。
senses.why: The black coating on such paper is made of carbon, so the paper took the element's name.
senses.whyCN: 这种纸上的黑色涂层由碳制成，于是纸张直接借用了元素的名字。

intro.en: Carbon is an old charcoal word that chemistry gave a precise new meaning.
intro.cn: carbon 是一个古老的「木炭」词，化学给了它精确的新含义。

items.en: carbo meant a piece of charcoal or a glowing coal.
items.cn: carbo 指一块木炭或烧红的炭。

items.en: French chemists used carbone for the element they had isolated from charcoal.
items.cn: 法国化学家用 carbone 称呼他们从木炭中分离出的元素。

items.en: English borrowed carbone as carbon during the chemical revolution.
items.cn: 在化学革命期间，英语借入 carbone，写作 carbon。

items.en: The word spread into compounds such as carbon dioxide and carbon paper.
items.cn: 这个词扩散到二氧化碳、复写纸等复合词中。

items.en: Today carbon is central to climate talk, as in carbon footprint and carbon emissions.
items.cn: 今天 carbon 是气候话题的核心词，如碳足迹与碳排放。

note.en: Carbon has a large chemical family, and it is also the name of several very different materials.
note.cn: carbon 有一个庞大的化学词族，同时也指几种外观差别很大的材料。

entries.definition: a salt containing carbon and oxygen
entries.definitionCN: 含碳和氧的盐类，由 carbon 加 -ate 构成。

entries.definition: relating to carbon, especially in acids
entries.definitionCN: 与碳有关的，尤指碳酸的。

entries.definition: to turn something into carbon or charcoal
entries.definitionCN: 使某物碳化、变成炭。

entries.definition: black material made by burning wood slowly
entries.definitionCN: 木材慢烧制成的黑色材料，与 carbon 的古义最接近。

entries.definition: a soft black form of carbon used in pencils
entries.definitionCN: 石墨，一种柔软的黑色碳单质，用于铅笔芯。

entries.definition: a very hard clear form of carbon
entries.definitionCN: 钻石，碳的一种极硬透明形态。

normalIntro.en: The element hides inside the old word for charcoal, and the family shows its many forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个元素躲在古老的「木炭」词里，而词族展示了它的多种形态。

normal.en: carbon comes from Latin carbo, charcoal, so the word is older than chemistry.
normal.cn: carbon 来自拉丁语 carbo（木炭），这个词比化学更古老。

normal.en: carbon dioxide and carbon monoxide name gases built on carbon.
normal.cn: carbon dioxide 与 carbon monoxide 都是以碳为基础的气体名称。

normal.en: carbon paper copies writing because its black layer is carbon.
normal.cn: 复写纸能复印字迹，是因为它的黑色涂层就是碳。

normal.en: carbon footprint measures the carbon a person or product leaves behind.
normal.cn: 碳足迹衡量一个人或一件产品留下的碳排放。

normal.en: Carbon is uncountable, so it takes no plural in ordinary use.
normal.cn: carbon 作元素名时不可数，日常使用没有复数。

abstract.en: Picture a blackened stick pulled from a fire, still warm.
abstract.cn: 想象一根从火里抽出的黑木棍，还带着余温。

abstract.en: Picture the same element as dull pencil lead and as a brilliant diamond.
abstract.cn: 想象同一种元素，一面是暗灰的铅笔芯，一面是璀璨的钻石。

abstract.en: Picture a dark layer under a sheet of paper catching every stroke of the pen.
abstract.cn: 想象纸下那层黑色材料，接住笔尖的每一次划动。

examples.en: Both diamond and graphite are made of carbon.
examples.cn: 钻石和石墨都由碳构成。

examples.en: Carbon is the basic building block of all living things.
examples.cn: 碳是一切生物的基本组成单元。

examples.en: The receipt was typed with carbon paper.
examples.cn: 那张收据是用复写纸打出来的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡本」——烧成炭的木本，剩下的黑色就是碳。

root: 拉丁语 carbo（木炭、炭火）→ 法语 carbone → 英语 carbon；同根词有 charcoal、carbonic。

sensesIntro.en: One element appears as charcoal, as diamond, and as the black layer of copying paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种元素，既以木炭出现，也以钻石出现，还以复写纸的黑色涂层出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: black charcoal left after fire, the visible trace of one element.
core.cn: 核心意象：火熄灭后留下的黑炭，是一种元素可见的痕迹。

branches.en: The chemical sense: the element shared by coal, diamonds, and living tissue.
branches.cn: 化学义：煤、钻石与生物组织共有的元素。

branches.en: The office sense: dark paper that transfers writing.
branches.cn: 办公义：能转印字迹的深色纸张。

branches.en: Compounds such as carbon dioxide and carbon fibre are built on the element.
branches.cn: 二氧化碳、碳纤维等复合词都以这一元素为基础。

branches.en: Climate language turns the element into a measure of human impact.
branches.cn: 气候话题把这一元素变成了衡量人类影响的指标。

branches.en: The copying sense survives mainly in carbon paper and carbon copy.
branches.cn: 复写义主要保留在复写纸与副本这两个说法里。

intro.en: Carbon is a base noun from Latin, and chemistry built a large family on it.
intro.cn: carbon 是来自拉丁语的基础名词，化学在它之上建起了一个大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin carbo, charcoal, is the source of carbon and of several chemical terms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 carbo（木炭）是 carbon 及若干化学术语的来源。

items.meaning: the element found in coal and diamonds
items.meaningCN: 碳，存在于煤和钻石中的元素
items.example: Carbon has six protons in each atom.
items.exampleCN: 每个碳原子有六个质子。

items.example: The rock is mostly calcium carbonate.
items.exampleCN: 这块岩石主要是碳酸钙。

items.example: Carbonic acid forms when gas dissolves in water.
items.exampleCN: 气体溶于水时形成碳酸。

items.example: The heat carbonized the outer layer of wood.

items.meaningCN: 含二氧化碳的，指碳酸饮料
items.example: She prefers carbonated water.
The city plans to decarbonize its buses.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市计划让公交车脱碳。

items.meaning: black material made by burning wood
items.example: They cooked over charcoal.
Carbo gave French carbone.

definition_en: a small piece of stiff paper or plastic used for writing, greeting, or playing
core_image: 一小片硬纸，上面写着字或印着图案
scene: 她把生日卡片放在桌上。She put the birthday card on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 card 是「卡片」（第 1 个义项：写有文字或印有图案的硬纸片）；句意是她把生日卡片放在桌上。

derivatives.zh: card 与 board 复合，义为「硬纸板」
card 与 holder 复合，义为「持卡人；卡套」
post 与 card 复合，义为「明信片」

senses.title: A small piece of stiff paper
senses.definition: a small piece of thick paper or plastic with writing or a picture on it
senses.definitionCN: 写有文字或印有图案的小块厚纸或塑料片
senses.example: He sent me a card from the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他从海边给我寄了一张卡片。
senses.why: Greek chartes named a leaf of papyrus, and the small stiff sheet kept that shape.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 chartes 指一片纸草，小块硬纸片保留了这种形状。

senses.title: One of a set used in games
senses.definition: one of a set of small cards with suits and numbers used for games
senses.definitionCN: 一套带有花色和点数、用于游戏的小卡片之一
senses.example: They played cards until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打牌打到半夜。
senses.why: Playing cards are simply small stiff sheets marked for a game, so the same word covers them.
senses.whyCN: 扑克牌就是印了记号、用于游戏的小硬纸片，所以同一个词就能涵盖。

intro.en: Card goes back to a Greek word for a sheet of papyrus, through Latin and French.
intro.cn: card 可追溯到希腊语中「一片纸草」的说法，经拉丁语和法语传来。

items.en: chartes named a sheet of papyrus used for writing.
items.cn: chartes 指书写用的一片纸草。

items.en: charta meant paper or a written document.
items.cn: charta 意为「纸」或「书面文件」。

items.en: carte named a card or a playing card in medieval France.
items.cn: 中古法语 carte 指卡片或纸牌。

items.en: English borrowed it as card, first for playing cards and notices.
items.cn: 英语借入为 card，最初指纸牌和告示。

items.en: The word spread to greeting cards, business cards, and bank cards.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到贺卡、名片和银行卡。

note.en: Card shares its paper root with chart and carton, and it sits beside other small printed objects.
note.cn: card 与 chart、carton 共享「纸」这个词根，同时和别的小型印刷物相邻。

entries.definition: a diagram or table that shows information
entries.definitionCN: 图表，与 card 同出拉丁语 charta（纸）。

entries.definition: a container made of thick paper or plastic
entries.definitionCN: 厚纸或塑料做的容器，同样源自 charta。

entries.definition: thick stiff paper used for boxes
entries.definitionCN: 做盒子用的硬纸板，由 card 与 board 复合而成。

entries.definition: a small piece of paper that shows you have paid
entries.definitionCN: 证明已付费的小纸片，与 card 同属小纸片。

entries.definition: a card for sending a short message by post
entries.definitionCN: 邮寄简短消息用的明信片。

entries.definition: a small label attached to something
entries.definitionCN: 系在物品上的小标签。

normalIntro.en: A card is a small stiff sheet, and the same sheet becomes a greeting, a bank card, or a playing card.
normalIntro.cn: card 就是一小片硬纸，同一片纸可以变成贺卡、银行卡或纸牌。

normal.en: card and chart share the Latin word charta, paper.
normal.cn: card 与 chart 共享拉丁语 charta（纸）。

normal.en: credit card and business card fix two everyday uses as whole phrases.
normal.cn: credit card 与 business card 把两种日常用途固定成整体说法。

normal.en: play cards uses the plural to mean a card game.
normal.cn: play cards 用复数表示「打牌」这项活动。

normal.en: postcard and cardboard are compounds built on card.
normal.cn: postcard 与 cardboard 都是以 card 为基础的复合词。

normal.en: The plural cards simply adds an s.
normal.cn: 复数 cards 只加一个 s。

abstract.en: Picture a small square of paper held between two fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象两指夹着一小片方形硬纸。

abstract.en: Picture a hand of cards fanned out and then folded together.
abstract.cn: 想象一手牌摊开成扇形，又合拢起来。

abstract.en: Picture a card sliding into a machine and a green light coming on.
abstract.cn: 想象一张卡滑进机器，绿灯亮起。

examples.en: She put the birthday card on the table.
examples.cn: 她把生日卡片放在桌上。

examples.en: He sent me a card from the coast.
examples.cn: 他从海边给我寄了一张卡片。

examples.en: They played cards until midnight.
examples.cn: 他们打牌打到半夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡得」——卡片太硬，卡得进钱包。

root: 希腊语 chartes（纸草片）→ 拉丁语 charta（纸）→ 古法语 carte → 英语 card；同根词有 chart、charter、carton。

sensesIntro.en: One small sheet of stiff paper serves writing, paying, and playing.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一小片硬纸，承担书写、支付和游戏三种用途。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small stiff sheet held in the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：拿在手里的一小片硬纸。

branches.en: The writing sense: greeting cards, business cards, and bank cards.
branches.cn: 书写义：贺卡、名片和银行卡。

branches.en: The game sense: one card in a deck with suits and numbers.
branches.cn: 游戏义：一副带花色和点数的牌中的一张。

branches.en: Compounds such as postcard and cardboard extend the paper idea.
branches.cn: postcard 与 cardboard 等复合词延伸了「纸片」这一概念。

branches.en: Both senses keep the same physical object, only the printing differs.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是同一个实物，只是印刷内容不同。

branches.en: play cards turns the object into the name of an activity.
branches.cn: play cards 把这个物件变成了活动的名称。

intro.en: Card is a base noun from Latin charta, paper, and it forms many compounds.
intro.cn: card 是源自拉丁语 charta（纸）的基础名词，能构成许多复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin charta, paper, links card with chart, charter, and carton.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 charta（纸）把 card 与 chart、charter、carton 连在一起。

items.meaning: a small stiff sheet for writing or games
items.example: The card was signed at the bottom.
She keeps old cards in a box.
items.exampleCN: 她把旧卡片收在盒子里。

items.example: The books arrived in a cardboard box.
items.exampleCN: 书装在一个硬纸箱里送到。

items.meaning: a person who owns a card, or a small case for cards
items.example: Cardholders get a small discount.
items.exampleCN: 持卡人可以享受小幅折扣。

items.example: He mailed a postcard from Rome.
items.exampleCN: 他从罗马寄了一张明信片。

items.example: The chart shows sales by month.
items.exampleCN: 这张图表显示每月销量。

items.example: Charta entered English through French.

items.meaning: a container made of thick paper
items.example: A carton of milk stood on the counter.

definition_en: thick stiff paper used for making boxes and simple models
core_image: 压厚的纸，硬得能自己立起来
scene: 他们把书装进硬纸箱里搬走。They packed the books into cardboard boxes and moved them.
sceneCN: 这里 cardboard 是「硬纸板」（第 1 个义项：做箱子用的厚纸板）；句意是他们把书装进硬纸箱里搬走。

derivatives.zh: cardboard 加 -y 构成，义为「像硬纸板一样的」
构成 cardboard 的第二个成分，义为「板」
构成 cardboard 的第一个成分，义为「卡片、硬纸片」

senses.title: Thick stiff paper for boxes
senses.definition: very thick stiff paper, often with layers pressed together
senses.definitionCN: 非常厚而硬的纸，通常由几层压合而成
senses.example: The package was wrapped in cardboard.
senses.exampleCN: 包裹用硬纸板包着。
senses.why: Card meant a stiff sheet and board meant a plank, so together they name a paper plank.
senses.whyCN: card 指硬纸片，board 指板，合起来就是「纸做的板」。

senses.title: Flat and lifeless, like a cutout
senses.definition: used about a character or story that seems flat and unconvincing
senses.definitionCN: 形容人物或故事扁平、不真实、缺乏生气
senses.example: The hero of the novel feels like a cardboard figure.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说的主人公像个纸板人，毫无生气。
senses.why: A cardboard cutout has shape but no life, and that image became a metaphor for flat writing.
senses.whyCN: 纸板剪影有形状却没有生命，这个形象就成了「人物扁平」的比喻。

intro.en: Cardboard is a plain compound of two old words, card and board, joined in the nineteenth century.
intro.cn: cardboard 是两个古老词语 card 与 board 的直白复合，在十九世纪合成为一个词。

items.en: bord meant a plank or a flat piece of wood, and later a flat surface.
items.cn: bord 指木板或一块平木头，后来也指平面。

items.en: card named a stiff sheet of paper used for writing or play.
items.cn: card 指用于书写或游戏的硬纸片。

items.en: Box makers began pressing layers of paper into stiff sheets and called the result cardboard.
items.cn: 制盒匠开始把纸层压成硬片，并把成品称为 cardboard。

items.en: Cheap cardboard boxes and toys made the word familiar in ordinary shops.
items.cn: 廉价纸箱和纸板玩具让这个词进入普通商店。

items.en: The adjective sense grew from cutouts, describing characters that are flat and lifeless.
items.cn: 形容词义从纸板剪影引申而来，形容扁平、没有生气的人物。

note.en: Cardboard is a transparent compound, and its neighbours are other thick paper products.
note.cn: cardboard 是词义透明的复合词，邻居是别的厚纸制品。

entries.definition: a small stiff sheet of paper
entries.definitionCN: 小片硬纸，是 cardboard 的第一个成分。

entries.definition: a long flat piece of wood or other hard material
entries.definitionCN: 长而平的木板或其他硬质板材，是第二个成分。

entries.definition: a container made of thick paper
entries.definitionCN: 厚纸做的容器，常由硬纸板制成。

entries.definition: thick paper used for packaging
entries.definitionCN: 包装用的厚纸板，与 cardboard 几乎同义。

entries.definition: stiff board made by pasting layers of paper
entries.definitionCN: 把纸层粘合而成的硬纸板，较旧的说法。

entries.definition: a container with flat sides, often made of cardboard
entries.definitionCN: 有平直侧面的容器，常用硬纸板制成。

normalIntro.en: Two easy pieces: card plus board equals a paper board.
normalIntro.cn: 两个简单部件：card 加 board 就是「纸做的板」。

normal.en: card gives the paper sheet, board gives the flat stiffness.
normal.cn: card 提供纸片，board 提供平板的硬度。

normal.en: cardboard box is the phrase you will meet most often.
normal.cn: cardboard box 是你最常遇到的搭配。

normal.en: The word is uncountable, so one says a sheet of cardboard.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数，所以说 a sheet of cardboard（一张硬纸板）。

normal.en: The adjective sense comes from cutouts: flat shape, no life.
normal.cn: 形容词义来自纸板剪影：只有形状，没有生命。

normal.en: carton is the box made from this material, a useful neighbour.
normal.cn: carton 是用这种材料做的盒子，是有用的邻词。

abstract.en: Picture a flat brown sheet standing upright without bending.
abstract.cn: 想象一张棕色平板自己立着，不会弯下去。

abstract.en: Picture a box folded from one piece of thick paper.
abstract.cn: 想象一个箱子由一整片厚纸折成。

abstract.en: Picture a life-size figure cut from board, smiling but not moving.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从纸板剪出的真人大小人形，笑着却不动。

examples.en: They packed the books into cardboard boxes and moved them.
examples.cn: 他们把书装进硬纸箱里搬走。

examples.en: The package was wrapped in cardboard.
examples.cn: 包裹用硬纸板包着。

examples.en: The hero of the novel feels like a cardboard figure.
examples.cn: 这部小说的主人公像个纸板人，毫无生气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「卡板」——卡片压成板，就是硬纸板。

root: 由 card（硬纸片）与 board（板）复合而成，十九世纪定型；card 源自拉丁语 charta（纸）。

sensesIntro.en: A material and a metaphor: stiff paper for boxes, and flatness for lifeless characters.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个材料，一个比喻：做箱子的硬纸，以及形容人物扁平的「纸板感」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: layers of paper pressed into a sheet stiff enough to stand.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸层被压成一张硬得能立起来的板。

branches.en: The material sense: thick paper used for boxes and models.
branches.cn: 材料义：做箱子和模型用的厚纸。

branches.en: The metaphorical sense: a figure with shape but no inner life.
branches.cn: 比喻义：有形状却没有内在生命的形象。

branches.en: cardboard box and cardboard tube name common objects made from it.
branches.cn: 硬纸箱与硬纸筒是这种材料的常见制品。

branches.en: Both senses rest on stiffness: strong enough to hold a shape, but hollow inside.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在「硬」上：足够撑出形状，里面却是空的。

branches.en: Critics call a flat character cardboard, borrowing the cutout image.
branches.cn: 评论者把扁平人物称为 cardboard，借用的正是纸板剪影的形象。

intro.en: Cardboard is a compound of card and board, not an affixed form.
intro.cn: cardboard 是 card 与 board 的复合词，不是加词缀构成的。

latinIntro.en: Only the first element has a Latin past: card goes back to charta, paper.
latinIntro.cn: 只有第一个成分有拉丁来源：card 可追溯到 charta（纸）。

items.example: The model was built from cardboard.
items.exampleCN: 这个模型是用硬纸板做的。

items.example: Write the address on the card.
The notice was pinned to the board.
Paperboard is sold by the sheet.

items.meaning: board made by pasting paper layers
items.example: The old book had a pasteboard cover.
items.exampleCN: 这本旧书是硬纸板封面。

items.example: He opened a carton of juice.
The box was too heavy to lift.
items.exampleCN: 这个箱子重得抬不起来。

items.example: The bread had a cardboardy texture.

definition_en: to feel that something is important and to give it attention and protection
core_image: 心里一直挂着一件事，放不下
scene: 她很在意孩子们有没有吃饱。She cares about whether the children have enough to eat.
sceneCN: 这里 cares 是 care 的第三人称单数，意为「在意、关心」（第 1 个义项：把某事放在心上）；句意是她很在意孩子们有没有吃饱。

derivatives.zh: care 加 -ful 构成，义为「小心的、仔细的」
care 加 -less 构成，义为「粗心的、不在意的」
care 加 -ing 构成，义为「有爱心的、体贴的」

senses.title: To feel that something matters
senses.definition: to feel interest in something and think it is important
senses.definitionCN: 对某事有兴趣，并认为它很重要
senses.example: He cares about what his students think.
senses.exampleCN: 他在意学生们的想法。
senses.why: Old English caru first meant anxiety, and concern is a milder form of the same feeling.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 caru 最初指忧虑，而「关心」正是同一种感觉较温和的形态。

senses.title: To look after someone
senses.definition: to look after a person or animal and keep them safe and well
senses.definitionCN: 照看某人或动物，使其安全健康
senses.example: She cares for her elderly father at home.
senses.exampleCN: 她在家里照顾年迈的父亲。
senses.why: Anxiety about someone turns into action, and the word comes to mean tending them.
senses.whyCN: 对某人的担忧会转化成行动，于是这个词引申为「照看、照料」。

senses.title: Attention paid to avoid mistakes
senses.definition: the attention you give to something so that nothing goes wrong
senses.definitionCN: 为了避免出错而付出的注意力
senses.example: Handle the glass with care.
senses.exampleCN: 拿这个玻璃杯要小心。
senses.why: If you care about an object, you watch it closely, and that watchfulness becomes care.
senses.whyCN: 在意一件东西，就会盯紧它，这种留神本身就是「小心」。

senses.title: A feeling of worry
senses.definition: a feeling of worry or anxiety about something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的担忧或焦虑
senses.example: The family was free from care for a while.
senses.exampleCN: 一家人暂时没有了忧虑。
senses.why: The oldest sense was sorrow and anxiety, and it survives in phrases such as free from care.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思就是悲伤与忧虑，它仍保留在 free from care 这类说法里。

intro.en: Care began as a word for anxiety and slowly turned toward protection and attention.
intro.cn: care 最初指忧虑，后来慢慢转向「保护」与「留意」。

items.en: caru meant sorrow, anxiety, and the burden of worry.
items.cn: caru 意为悲伤、忧虑和担忧的重负。

items.en: The verb cearian meant to be anxious about something.
items.cn: 动词 cearian 意为「为某事担忧」。

items.en: care widened from anxiety to protective attention and carefulness.
items.cn: care 从忧虑扩展到保护性的关注与小心。

items.en: Fixed phrases such as take care of settled the sense of looking after.
items.cn: take care of 这类固定说法确立了「照料」这一义项。

items.en: Today care about names emotional concern, while health care names a whole system.
items.cn: 今天 care about 指情感上的关心，而 health care 指整套医疗体系。

note.en: Care is the base of a large family, and its near meanings separate worry from looking after.
note.cn: care 是一个大词族的基础，近义词则把「担忧」与「照料」区分开。

entries.definition: giving attention so that nothing goes wrong
entries.definitionCN: 小心谨慎的、仔细的，由 care 加 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: not giving enough attention
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的、不在意的，由 care 加 -less 构成。

entries.definition: kind and attentive to others
entries.definitionCN: 有爱心、体贴人的。

entries.definition: a feeling of worry, or to be about something important
entries.definitionCN: 担忧，或与重要之事相关，对应第一和第四义项。

entries.definition: to keep thinking about problems
entries.definitionCN: 反复想着问题而担心。

entries.definition: to look after someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 照料某人或某物，对应第二个义项。

normalIntro.en: The oldest meaning is worry; every later sense grows out of holding something in mind.
normalIntro.cn: 最古老的意思是担忧；后来每个义项都从「心里挂着某事」长出来。

normal.en: care about means the thing stays in your mind.
normal.cn: care about 就是那件事一直留在你心里。

normal.en: care for turns that concern into action: feeding, nursing, protecting.
normal.cn: care for 把关心变成行动：喂饭、护理、保护。

normal.en: take care of is the fixed phrase for looking after someone or something.
normal.cn: take care of 是「照料某人或某物」的固定说法。

normal.en: with care adds the sense of caution to an action.
normal.cn: with care 给动作添上「谨慎」的意思。

normal.en: careful and careless split the family into attention and its absence.
normal.cn: careful 与 careless 把词族分成「留意」和「缺乏留意」两边。

abstract.en: Picture a small weight hanging inside the chest, never quite still.
abstract.cn: 想象胸口挂着一个很小的重物，始终不安稳。

abstract.en: Picture a hand resting on a sleeping child's back to check the breathing.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手放在熟睡孩子的背上，探一探呼吸。

abstract.en: Picture carrying a full cup across a room without spilling a drop.
abstract.cn: 想象端着一只满杯穿过房间，一滴也不洒。

examples.en: She cares about whether the children have enough to eat.
examples.cn: 她很在意孩子们有没有吃饱。

examples.en: She cares for her elderly father at home.
examples.cn: 她在家里照顾年迈的父亲。

examples.en: Handle the glass with care.
examples.cn: 拿这个玻璃杯要小心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开尔」——心里开着一个小小的口子，一直惦记着。

root: 古英语 caru（忧虑、挂念）与动词 cearian（担心）；同源词有 careful、careless、caring。

sensesIntro.en: Worry, concern, protection, and caution are four stages of the same mental grip.
sensesIntro.cn: 担忧、关心、照料、谨慎，是同一份「心里放不下」的四个阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held in the mind and never quite put down.
core.cn: 核心意象：某件事被放在心里，始终放不下。

branches.en: The emotional sense: something matters to you.
branches.cn: 情感义：某件事对你很重要。

branches.en: The active sense: concern becomes feeding, nursing, and protecting.
branches.cn: 行动义：关心转化为喂养、护理与保护。

branches.en: The cautious sense: attention applied to avoid mistakes.
branches.cn: 谨慎义：为避免出错而投入的注意力。

branches.en: The oldest sense: plain worry and sorrow.
branches.cn: 最古老的义项：单纯的忧虑与悲伤。

branches.en: All three active senses begin with the same grip of attention.
branches.cn: 三个主动义项都始于同一种「注意力抓住不放」。

intro.en: Care is a native base word; suffixes -ful, -less, and -ing build its main family.
intro.cn: care 是本族基础词，后缀 -ful、-less、-ing 构成它的主要词族。

latinIntro.en: Care has no Latin root: it comes from Old English, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: care 没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.meaning: to be concerned, or attention and protection
items.example: They care about the local school.

items.meaning: he, she, or it is concerned
items.example: She cares deeply about animals.
He cared for his mother for years.

items.meaning: looking after others, or kind and attentive
items.example: Nursing is a caring profession.
items.exampleCN: 护理是一门关怀人的职业。

items.example: Be careful with the knife.
A careless mistake cost them the game.
items.exampleCN: 一个粗心的失误让他们输掉了比赛。

items.meaning: a person who looks after someone
items.example: The caregiver visits twice a day.
Caru is the oldest recorded form.
items.exampleCN: caru 是最早有记录的形式。

definition_en: the job or series of jobs that a person does over a long period of life
core_image: 一条越跑越宽的跑道，人一直在上面往前
scene: 她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。She began her career in journalism.
sceneCN: 这里 career 是「职业生涯」（第 1 个义项：长期从事的工作历程）；句意是她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。

derivatives.zh: career 加 -ist 构成，义为「一味追求升迁的人」
career 加 -ism 构成，义为「追逐个人事业成功」

senses.title: The work a person does over years
senses.definition: the profession or occupation that a person follows for much of their life
senses.definitionCN: 一个人一生中大部分时间从事的专业或工作
senses.example: Teaching became his career after graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 毕业后教书成了他的职业。
senses.why: Career first meant a racecourse, and a working life came to be seen as a course run over years.
senses.whyCN: career 最初指跑道，而人的工作历程被看成一条跑过多年的赛道。

senses.title: The whole course of working life
senses.definition: the whole period of a person's working life, with its progress and changes
senses.definitionCN: 一个人工作生活的整个时期，包括其中的进展与变化
senses.example: Her career spanned three decades and two continents.
senses.exampleCN: 她的生涯横跨三十年、两个大洲。
senses.why: A course has a start and a finish, so career also names the full span rather than one job.
senses.whyCN: 跑道有起点和终点，所以 career 也指整段历程，而不只是某一份工作。

intro.en: Career began as a word for a racetrack, then became the track of a working life.
intro.cn: career 起初指赛马跑道，后来变成「工作人生的跑道」。

items.en: carrus named a wheeled wagon, the source of many words about vehicles and tracks.
items.cn: carrus 指带轮的车，是许多车辆与道路词的来源。

items.en: carriere meant a racecourse or the track on which horses ran.
items.cn: carriere 指赛马场或马匹奔跑的跑道。

items.en: English borrowed career for a racecourse and for a galloping course.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 career，指跑道与疾驰的路线。

items.en: The word shifted from a physical track to the course of a person's public life.
items.cn: 这个词从实体的跑道转指一个人公共生活的历程。

items.en: Today career means the profession itself and the whole span of working life.
items.cn: 今天 career 既指职业本身，也指整个工作生涯。

note.en: Career is a descendant of the wagon word car, and it sits beside other names for work.
note.cn: career 是「马车」一词 car 的后代，同时和别的「工作」名称相邻。

entries.definition: a road vehicle with an engine
entries.definitionCN: 汽车，与 career 同出拉丁语 carrus。

entries.definition: a railway car or a horse-drawn vehicle
entries.definitionCN: 火车车厢或马车，与 career 同根。

entries.definition: a two-wheeled vehicle pulled by horses in ancient races
entries.definitionCN: 古代赛车上用的双轮马车，同样源自 carrus。

entries.definition: a job requiring special training
entries.definitionCN: 需要专门训练的职业，最贴近 career 的第一义。

entries.definition: the kind of work a person does
entries.definitionCN: 一个人所从事的工作类别，较正式的用词。

entries.definition: a particular paid position
entries.definitionCN: 一份具体的有薪职位，时间跨度比 career 短。

normalIntro.en: The racetrack image makes the word easy: a career is the course you run for years.
normalIntro.cn: 跑道的画面让这个词很好记：career 就是你跑了很多年的那条赛道。

normal.en: career comes from carriere, a racecourse, built on the wagon word carrus.
normal.cn: career 来自 carriere（跑道），建立在「马车」一词 carrus 之上。

normal.en: A racecourse has a start and a direction, just like a working life.
normal.cn: 跑道有起点和方向，工作人生也一样。

normal.en: career path and career choice both use the road metaphor directly.
normal.cn: career path 与 career choice 都直接沿用了「道路」这个比喻。

normal.en: The phrase launch a career treats work as a vehicle setting off.
normal.cn: launch a career 把事业看成一辆出发的车。

normal.en: The plural careers covers several people's working lives.
normal.cn: 复数 careers 指多人的职业生涯。

abstract.en: Picture a long track curving out of sight, with footprints already on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长长的跑道弯出视线，上面已有脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a horse cart on the same track, then a car, then a person walking.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条跑道上先是马车，再是汽车，最后是一个步行的人。

abstract.en: Picture a single line drawn through many years on a calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象在日历上画一条穿过许多年的线。

examples.en: She began her career in journalism.
examples.cn: 她在新闻行业开始了自己的职业生涯。

examples.en: Teaching became his career after graduation.
examples.cn: 毕业后教书成了他的职业。

examples.en: Her career spanned three decades and two continents.
examples.cn: 她的生涯横跨三十年、两个大洲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可瑞尔」——在跑道上一直往前跑，就是职业生涯。

root: 拉丁语 carrus（车）→ 古法语 carriere（跑道）→ 英语 career（跑道，后指人生历程）。

sensesIntro.en: One metaphor, two reaches: the profession itself and the whole course it runs on.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个比喻，两种跨度：职业本身，以及它所在的那整条跑道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a racetrack stretching forward, with someone running along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条向前延伸的跑道，有人正在上面奔跑。

branches.en: The job sense: the profession a person settles into.
branches.cn: 工作义：一个人长期从事的职业。

branches.en: The span sense: the whole run from first job to retirement.
branches.cn: 跨度义：从第一份工作到退休的整段历程。

branches.en: Both senses borrow the shape of a track: direction, progress, and distance covered.
branches.cn: 两个义项都借用了跑道的形状：方向、进展和已跑过的距离。

branches.en: career development treats the job as something that can be built stage by stage.
branches.cn: career development 把职业看成可以分阶段搭建的东西。

branches.en: A career can be long or short, smooth or broken, like any course.
branches.cn: 生涯可长可短、可顺可断，就像任何一条跑道。

intro.en: Career is a base noun; the suffix -ist and -ism build its small modern family.
intro.cn: career 是基础名词，后缀 -ist 与 -ism 构成它不大的现代词族。

latinIntro.en: The root goes back to Latin carrus, a wagon, which also gives car and carriage.
latinIntro.cn: 词根可追溯到拉丁语 carrus（车），它也带来 car 与 carriage。

items.meaning: a profession or the course of working life
items.example: He changed careers at forty.
The school advises students on careers.
items.exampleCN: 学校为学生提供职业指导。

items.meaning: a person who puts career success first
items.meaningCN: 一心追求事业升迁的人
items.example: He was seen as a careerist.
items.exampleCN: 他被看作一个只顾往上爬的人。

items.meaning: the pursuit of personal career success
items.meaningCN: 追逐个人事业成功的作风
items.example: Critics blamed careerism for the decision.
items.exampleCN: 批评者把这一决定归咎于追逐名利。

items.example: Carrus is the root of career.
items.exampleCN: carrus 是 career 的词根。

items.example: The car waited outside.

items.meaning: a railway car or horse-drawn vehicle
items.example: The carriage was empty.
The chariot raced around the track.

definition_en: giving attention to what you do so that nothing goes wrong
core_image: 端着一杯满水，眼睛一直盯着杯沿
scene: 过马路时要小心。Be careful when you cross the road.
sceneCN: 这里 careful 是「小心的」（第 1 个义项：注意避免危险或错误）；句意是过马路时要小心。

derivatives.zh: careful 加 -ly 构成，义为「小心地、仔细地」
careful 加 -ness 构成，义为「谨慎、细心」
careful 的基础词，义为「关心、小心」

senses.title: Avoiding danger or mistakes
senses.definition: paying attention so that you do not hurt yourself or damage something
senses.definitionCN: 集中注意力，以免伤到自己或损坏东西
senses.example: Be careful with the hot pan.
senses.exampleCN: 小心那个烫锅。
senses.why: Care plus -ful means full of care, and care first meant anxious attention.
senses.whyCN: care 加 -ful 意为「充满关切」，而 care 最初指带着焦虑的留意。

senses.title: Doing something with attention to detail
senses.definition: done with thought and attention so that details are correct
senses.definitionCN: 做事时用心留意，使细节都正确
senses.example: She gave the report a careful reading.
senses.exampleCN: 她把报告仔细读了一遍。
senses.why: The same watchfulness that avoids danger also catches small errors in work.
senses.whyCN: 用来避开危险的同一份留心，也能在工作里发现细小错误。

intro.en: Careful is a native compound: care plus the suffix -ful, meaning full of care.
intro.cn: careful 是本族语的复合形式：care 加上后缀 -ful，意为「充满关切」。

items.en: caru meant sorrow and anxious attention.
items.cn: caru 意为悲伤与焦虑的留意。

items.en: care added the sense of protective attention and caution.
items.cn: care 增加了保护性关注与谨慎的含义。

items.en: carefull appeared, meaning full of care, often in the older sense of anxious.
items.cn: carefull 出现，意为「充满关切的」，常带较古的「忧虑」意味。

items.en: The meaning settled on attentive and cautious rather than worried.
items.cn: 词义稳定为「留心的、谨慎的」，而不再是「忧虑的」。

items.en: Today careful covers both avoiding danger and attending to detail.
items.cn: 今天的 careful 既指避开危险，也指注意细节。

note.en: Careful belongs to the care family, and its near meanings split caution from thoroughness.
note.cn: careful 属于 care 词族，近义词把「谨慎」与「细致」区分开。

entries.definition: not giving enough attention
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的、不在意的，由 care 加 -less 构成，是 careful 的反义形式。

entries.definition: in a careful way
entries.definitionCN: 小心地、仔细地，由 careful 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: concern, protection, or caution
entries.definitionCN: 关心、照料或小心，是 careful 的基础词。

entries.definition: avoiding danger or risk
entries.definitionCN: 避开危险或风险的，更强调「防风险」。

entries.definition: paying close attention to something
entries.definitionCN: 专注留意的，更贴近「仔细」这一义。

entries.definition: complete, with every detail checked
entries.definitionCN: 彻底的、每个细节都检查过的。

normalIntro.en: Care plus -ful is easy to see: full of care means full of attention.
normalIntro.cn: care 加 -ful 一眼可见：充满关切，就是充满留意。

normal.en: careful is simply care plus the suffix -ful, full of.
normal.cn: careful 就是 care 加后缀 -ful（充满…的）。

normal.en: The opposite is careless, built with -less, without.
normal.cn: 反义词是 careless，用 -less（没有…的）构成。

normal.en: The adverb carefully adds -ly and keeps the same meaning.
normal.cn: 副词 carefully 加 -ly，意思不变。

normal.en: The pattern be careful with takes a noun, while be careful to takes a verb.
normal.cn: be careful with 后接名词，be careful to 后接动词。

normal.en: Careful uses more and most rather than -er and -est.
normal.cn: careful 的比较级和最高级用 more、most，而不是 -er、-est。

abstract.en: Picture a full cup carried across a room without spilling.
abstract.cn: 想象端着一杯满水穿过房间，一滴不洒。

abstract.en: Picture eyes moving slowly along a line of print to catch every word.
abstract.cn: 想象目光沿着一行字慢慢移动，不放过每个词。

abstract.en: Picture a hand hovering just above a hot stove.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手悬在热炉上方，随时准备缩回。

examples.en: Be careful when you cross the road.
examples.cn: 过马路时要小心。

examples.en: Be careful with the hot pan.
examples.cn: 小心那个烫锅。

examples.en: She gave the report a careful reading.
examples.cn: 她把报告仔细读了一遍。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开尔福」——心里装满了关怀，做事自然就小心。

root: care（关心、小心）+ -ful（充满…的）；care 源自古英语 caru（忧虑、挂念）。

sensesIntro.en: One watchfulness, two directions: guarding against harm and checking every detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种留心，两个方向：防住伤害，检查细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes fixed on a delicate thing while the hands move slowly.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼睛盯着易碎之物，双手慢慢移动。

branches.en: The safety sense: attention kept on possible harm.
branches.cn: 安全义：注意力放在可能的伤害上。

branches.en: The accuracy sense: attention kept on details and correctness.
branches.cn: 准确义：注意力放在细节与正确性上。

branches.en: Both senses are the same care, pointed at danger or at detail.
branches.cn: 两个义项是同一种 care，只是分别指向危险与细节。

branches.en: careful driver and be careful with are the everyday patterns.
branches.cn: careful driver 与 be careful with 是日常最常见的用法。

branches.en: careful reading and careful planning show the detail sense in action.
branches.cn: careful reading 与 careful planning 展示了「细致」义的用法。

intro.en: Careful is care plus the suffix -ful, and it in turn takes -ly and -ness.
intro.cn: careful 是 care 加后缀 -ful，它本身又能加 -ly 与 -ness。

latinIntro.en: Careful is native English, so there is no Latin root to list.
latinIntro.cn: careful 是英语本族词，因此没有可列的拉丁词根。

items.example: She is careful with money.
Read the instructions carefully.
His carefulness saved the experiment.
items.exampleCN: 他的细心救了这次实验。

items.example: A careless reply upset her.
items.exampleCN: 一句粗心的回复让她难过。

items.example: Take care on the stairs.
They spent a carefree summer by the sea.
items.exampleCN: 他们在海边度过了一个无忧无虑的夏天。

items.example: He is a caring teacher.
items.exampleCN: 他是一位关心学生的老师。

items.example: Caru is the oldest form of care.
items.exampleCN: caru 是 care 最古老的形式。

definition_en: in a way that shows attention and avoids mistakes or danger
core_image: 放慢动作，一步一步把事做稳
scene: 她小心地把杯子放回架子上。She carefully placed the cup back on the shelf.
sceneCN: 这里 carefully 是「小心地」（第 1 个义项：动作谨慎、避免碰坏东西）；句意是她小心地把杯子放回架子上。

derivatives.zh: carefully 的基础形容词，义为「小心的、仔细的」
careful 加 -ness 构成，义为「谨慎、细心」
整个词族的基础词，义为「关心、小心」

senses.title: In a way that avoids harm
senses.definition: with attention so that nothing is broken, hurt, or lost
senses.definitionCN: 带着注意力，使东西不被弄坏、人不受伤害
senses.example: He carried the vase carefully to the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他小心地把花瓶搬到桌上。
senses.why: The adverb simply applies careful to an action, and careful means full of care.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词只是把 careful 用在动作上，而 careful 本义是「充满关切」。

senses.title: With attention to detail
senses.definition: with close attention so that every detail is correct
senses.definitionCN: 密切关注，使每个细节都正确
senses.example: Read the question carefully before you answer.
senses.exampleCN: 回答之前先仔细读题。
senses.why: The same attention that protects objects also protects accuracy in thought and work.
senses.whyCN: 保护物品的同一份注意力，也保护思考与工作中的准确性。

intro.en: Carefully is a transparent adverb: careful plus -ly, built on the old word care.
intro.cn: carefully 是词义透明的副词：careful 加 -ly，根基是古老的 care。

items.en: caru meant sorrow and anxious attention.
items.cn: caru 意为悲伤与焦虑的留意。

items.en: care took on the sense of protective attention and caution.
items.cn: care 获得了保护性关注与谨慎的含义。

items.en: carefull appeared as an adjective meaning full of care.
items.cn: 形容词 carefull 出现，意为「充满关切的」。

items.en: The adverb carefully was formed by adding -ly, as with most English adjectives.
items.cn: 副词 carefully 由加 -ly 构成，和多数英语形容词一样。

items.en: Today carefully covers both physical caution and mental thoroughness.
items.cn: 今天的 carefully 同时覆盖动作上的谨慎和思考上的细致。

note.en: Carefully is the adverb of care, and its near meanings differ in what kind of attention they name.
note.cn: carefully 是 care 词族的副词，近义词的区别在于强调哪种留意。

entries.definition: giving attention to avoid mistakes
entries.definitionCN: 小心的、仔细的，是 carefully 的基础形容词。

entries.definition: not giving enough attention
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的，carefully 的反义对应词。

entries.definition: the quality of being careful
entries.definitionCN: 谨慎、细心，是这一词族的抽象名词。

entries.definition: in a way that avoids risk
entries.definitionCN: 谨慎地、避开风险地，更强调防危险。

entries.definition: with close attention
entries.definitionCN: 专注地、留心地，更贴近「仔细」义。

entries.definition: completely, with every detail checked
entries.definitionCN: 彻底地、每个细节都检查到地。

normalIntro.en: Add -ly to careful and the adverb is done; the meaning stays full of care.
normalIntro.cn: 在 careful 后加 -ly 就得到这个副词，意思仍是「充满关切」。

normal.en: carefully is careful plus -ly, the standard way to make an adverb.
normal.cn: carefully 是 careful 加 -ly，构成副词的标准方式。

normal.en: The base careful is care plus -ful, full of care.
normal.cn: 基础词 careful 是 care 加 -ful，意为「充满关切」。

normal.en: The opposite is carelessly, built on careless.
normal.cn: 反义词是 carelessly，来自 careless。

normal.en: It often sits before a verb: carefully placed, carefully worded.
normal.cn: 它常放在动词前：carefully placed（小心放置）、carefully worded（措辞谨慎）。

normal.en: As an adverb it has no comparative form of its own; more carefully does the work.
normal.cn: 副词本身没有 -er 形式，比较级用 more carefully。

abstract.en: Picture a hand slowing down just before it sets a glass on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手在把杯子放上桌前，忽然慢了下来。

abstract.en: Picture a finger moving under each line of print as the eyes follow.
abstract.cn: 想象手指在每一行字下移动，眼睛跟着走。

abstract.en: Picture a person testing each step of a dark staircase with one foot.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人用一只脚试探黑楼梯的每一级。

examples.en: She carefully placed the cup back on the shelf.
examples.cn: 她小心地把杯子放回架子上。

examples.en: Read the question carefully before you answer.
examples.cn: 回答之前先仔细读题。

examples.en: The plan was carefully worded to avoid blame.
examples.cn: 这份计划的措辞经过仔细推敲，以避免被指责。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开尔弗利」——心里挂着事，动作就慢而稳。

root: careful + -ly；care 源自古英语 caru（忧虑、挂念），-ful 意为「充满…的」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb, two jobs: moving safely and reading closely.
sensesIntro.cn: 一个副词，两项工作：动作上求安全，阅读上求准确。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: movement slowed down by attention.
core.cn: 核心意象：因为留心而放慢的动作。

branches.en: The safety sense: handling things so they do not break.
branches.cn: 安全义：拿放东西时不让它损坏。

branches.en: The accuracy sense: reading and thinking without skipping details.
branches.cn: 准确义：阅读与思考时不漏掉细节。

branches.en: Both senses describe the same slowed, focused action.
branches.cn: 两个义项描写的都是同一种放慢而专注的动作。

branches.en: drive carefully and handle carefully are the common warnings.
branches.cn: 小心驾驶、小心拿放是最常见的提醒说法。

branches.en: carefully planned and carefully worded show the detail sense.
branches.cn: 精心策划与措辞谨慎展示了「细致」这一面。

intro.en: Carefully is built from care by adding -ful and then -ly.
intro.cn: carefully 由 care 先加 -ful、再加 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The whole family is native English, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都是英语本族词，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Hold the bowl carefully.
She is careful with details.
His carefulness impressed the judge.
A careless step broke the branch.
He carelessly left the door open.
She did it with great care.
items.exampleCN: 她非常小心地做了这件事。

items.example: The children ran carefree across the field.
items.exampleCN: 孩子们无忧无虑地跑过田野。

items.example: Caru is the old root of the family.
items.exampleCN: caru 是这个词族的古老词根。

definition_en: not giving enough attention, so that mistakes or damage happen
core_image: 手里的东西滑出去，人却没有察觉
scene: 一个粗心的错误让整份报告作废。One careless mistake made the whole report useless.
sceneCN: 这里 careless 是「粗心的」（第 1 个义项：注意力不足而犯错）；句意是一个粗心的错误让整份报告作废。

derivatives.zh: careless 加 -ly 构成，义为「粗心地、漫不经心地」
careless 加 -ness 构成，义为「粗心、疏忽」
careless 的基础词，义为「关心、小心」

senses.title: Not paying enough attention
senses.definition: not paying enough attention, so that mistakes are made
senses.definitionCN: 注意力不够，因而出现错误
senses.example: A careless driver ran the red light.
senses.exampleCN: 一个疏忽的司机闯了红灯。
senses.why: Careless is care plus -less, literally without care, and without care mistakes follow.
senses.whyCN: careless 是 care 加 -less，字面就是「没有关切」，没有关切就容易出错。

senses.title: Not worried or concerned
senses.definition: not showing concern about something, sometimes in a relaxed way
senses.definitionCN: 对某事不表示关切，有时带轻松随意之意
senses.example: She was careless of what others thought.
senses.exampleCN: 她不在乎别人怎么想。
senses.why: The oldest sense was free from care, and that relaxed indifference survives beside the negative sense.
senses.whyCN: 较早的意思是「没有忧虑」，这份轻松的满不在乎与贬义的「粗心」并存至今。

intro.en: Careless literally means without care, and its meaning moved from freedom from worry to lack of attention.
intro.cn: careless 字面是「没有关切」，词义从「无忧」滑向「缺乏注意」。

items.en: caru meant sorrow and anxious attention.
items.cn: caru 意为悲伤与焦虑的留意。

items.en: care added the sense of protective attention.
items.cn: care 增加了保护性关注的意思。

items.en: careless first meant free from care, untroubled and light-hearted.
items.cn: careless 最初意为「没有忧虑的、轻松愉快的」。

items.en: The sense darkened toward not paying attention and therefore making mistakes.
items.cn: 词义转向「不注意」，并因此带上「会出错」的贬义。

items.en: Today careless mostly criticizes inattention, while the calm sense survives in fixed phrases.
items.cn: 今天 careless 多批评「不注意」，而「安然不在意」的意思只在少数固定说法里保留。

note.en: Careless is the negative member of the care family, and its near meanings range from negligent to reckless.
note.cn: careless 是 care 词族中的否定成员，近义词从「疏忽」到「鲁莽」不等。

entries.definition: giving attention to avoid mistakes
entries.definitionCN: 小心的、仔细的，是 careless 的反义对应词。

entries.definition: in a careless way
entries.definitionCN: 粗心地、漫不经心地，由 careless 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: lack of attention
entries.definitionCN: 粗心、疏忽，是这一词族的抽象名词。

entries.definition: failing to give proper care to a duty
entries.definitionCN: 对职责未尽应有注意的，较正式。

entries.definition: acting without thinking about danger
entries.definitionCN: 不顾危险行动的，程度比 careless 更重。

entries.definition: done in a messy, careless way
entries.definitionCN: 马虎的、草率的，口语色彩较强。

normalIntro.en: The suffix tells the story: -less means without, so careless means without care.
normalIntro.cn: 后缀说明了问题：-less 意为「没有」，careless 就是「没有 care」。

normal.en: careless is care plus -less, literally without care.
normal.cn: careless 是 care 加 -less，字面就是「没有关切」。

normal.en: The opposite is careful, built with -ful.
normal.cn: 反义词是 careful，用 -ful 构成。

normal.en: careless mistake is the most common collocation and shows the result of inattention.
normal.cn: careless mistake 是最常见的搭配，点出了不注意的后果。

normal.en: careless about means indifferent, the older and softer sense.
normal.cn: careless about 意为「对…不在意」，是较旧、较温和的义项。

normal.en: The adverb carelessly and the noun carelessness complete the family.
normal.cn: 副词 carelessly 与名词 carelessness 补全了这个词族。

abstract.en: Picture a cup sliding off a table while the owner looks away.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子正从桌上滑落，而主人看向别处。

abstract.en: Picture a signature written so fast that the letters blur together.
abstract.cn: 想象签名写得太快，字母糊成一片。

abstract.en: Picture a gate left open behind someone walking away.
abstract.cn: 想象有人走开，身后留下一扇没关的门。

examples.en: One careless mistake made the whole report useless.
examples.cn: 一个粗心的错误让整份报告作废。

examples.en: A careless driver ran the red light.
examples.cn: 一个疏忽的司机闯了红灯。

examples.en: She was careless of what others thought.
examples.cn: 她不在乎别人怎么想。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开尔莱斯」——心里没有 care，做事就丢三落四。

root: care（关心、小心）+ -less（没有…的）；care 源自古英语 caru（忧虑、挂念）。

sensesIntro.en: Without care can mean either a relaxed freedom from worry or a damaging lack of attention.
sensesIntro.cn: 「没有关切」既可以是轻松无忧，也可以是有害的注意力缺失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand letting go of something without noticing.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手没察觉地松开了东西。

branches.en: The fault sense: attention missing, so errors appear.
branches.cn: 过失义：注意力缺位，于是错误出现。

branches.en: The calm sense: not troubled by what others think.
branches.cn: 淡然义：不为别人的看法所扰。

branches.en: careless driving and careless mistake show the fault sense in fixed phrases.
branches.cn: careless driving 与 careless mistake 用固定搭配展示过失义。

branches.en: Both senses come from the same absence of care, judged differently.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自「没有 care」，只是评价不同。

branches.en: careless of danger describes someone untroubled by risk rather than merely sloppy.
branches.cn: careless of danger 形容的是不在乎风险，而不只是马虎。

intro.en: Careless is care plus the privative suffix -less, without.
intro.cn: careless 是 care 加表「缺少」的后缀 -less。

latinIntro.en: The family is native English, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族是英语本族词，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: His careless answer annoyed the teacher.
items.exampleCN: 他粗心的回答让老师不快。

items.example: She carelessly dropped the keys.
items.exampleCN: 她漫不经心地弄掉了钥匙。

items.example: The accident was blamed on carelessness.
items.exampleCN: 这起事故被归咎于疏忽。

items.example: She handled it with care.
Be careful with the glass.
They had a carefree afternoon.
items.exampleCN: 他们度过了一个无忧无虑的下午。

items.example: He gave an uncaring shrug.
items.exampleCN: 他漠不关心地耸了耸肩。

items.example: Caru is the old root of care.
items.exampleCN: caru 是 care 的古老词根。

definition_en: in a way that shows too little attention or concern
core_image: 手一松，东西直接掉下去
scene: 他把湿伞随手丢在地板上。He carelessly threw the wet umbrella on the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 carelessly 是「漫不经心地」（第 1 个义项：动作缺少注意）；句意是他把湿伞随手丢在地板上。

derivatives.zh: carelessly 的基础形容词，义为「粗心的」
careless 加 -ness 构成，义为「粗心、疏忽」
整个词族的基础词，义为「关心、小心」

senses.title: In a way that causes mistakes
senses.definition: with too little attention, so that errors or damage are likely
senses.definitionCN: 注意力不足，容易造成错误或损坏
senses.example: He carelessly left the gate open all night.
senses.exampleCN: 他粗心地把门开了一整夜。
senses.why: The adverb applies careless to an action, and careless means without care.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把 careless 用在动作上，而 careless 意为「没有关切」。

senses.title: In a casual, unconcerned way
senses.definition: in a relaxed way that shows little concern for the result
senses.definitionCN: 轻松随意，对结果不太在意
senses.example: She carelessly waved away the warning.
senses.exampleCN: 她漫不经心地挥挥手，把警告打发掉了。
senses.why: The older sense of free from care survives as a casual lightness rather than a fault.
senses.whyCN: 较早的「无忧」义仍以「随意轻松」的形式存在，而不一定构成过失。

intro.en: Carelessly is careless plus -ly, and the whole family grows from the old word care.
intro.cn: carelessly 是 careless 加 -ly，整个词族从古老的 care 生长出来。

items.en: caru meant sorrow and anxious attention.
items.cn: caru 意为悲伤与焦虑的留意。

items.en: care gained the sense of protective attention.
items.cn: care 获得了保护性关注的意思。

items.en: careless appeared, first meaning free from care and untroubled.
items.cn: careless 出现，最初意为「没有忧虑、安然自在」。

items.en: carelessly was formed with -ly as the adverb of the newer sense, without attention.
items.cn: carelessly 由 -ly 构成，作为「缺乏注意」这一较新义项的副词。

items.en: Today carelessly usually criticizes inattention, though the casual sense remains.
items.cn: 今天 carelessly 多批评「不注意」，但「随意」的意思仍然存在。

note.en: Carelessly is the adverb of the careless branch, and its neighbours differ in how blameworthy the action is.
note.cn: carelessly 属于 careless 这一支的副词，近义词的区别在于过失程度的轻重。

entries.definition: not giving enough attention
entries.definitionCN: 粗心的，是 carelessly 的基础形容词。

entries.definition: lack of attention
entries.definitionCN: 粗心、疏忽，是这个副词对应的名词。

entries.definition: with attention and caution
entries.definitionCN: 小心地、仔细地，正好是 carelessly 的反义副词。

entries.definition: in a way that fails to give proper care
entries.definitionCN: 疏忽地、未尽应有注意地，较正式。

entries.definition: without thinking about danger
entries.definitionCN: 鲁莽地、不顾危险地，程度比 carelessly 更重。

entries.definition: in a messy and careless way
entries.definitionCN: 马虎地、草率地，口语色彩较强。

normalIntro.en: Careless plus -ly makes the adverb; the -less in the middle means without.
normalIntro.cn: careless 加 -ly 构成副词，中间的 -less 意为「没有」。

normal.en: carelessly is careless plus -ly.
normal.cn: carelessly 就是 careless 加 -ly。

normal.en: careless itself is care plus -less, without care.
normal.cn: careless 本身是 care 加 -less，意为「没有关切」。

normal.en: The opposite adverb is carefully.
normal.cn: 反义副词是 carefully。

normal.en: It often follows a verb: drive carelessly, speak carelessly.
normal.cn: 它常跟在动词后：drive carelessly、speak carelessly。

normal.en: As an adverb it has no -er form; more carelessly is used instead.
normal.cn: 副词没有 -er 形式，比较级用 more carelessly。

abstract.en: Picture an umbrella dropped on the floor and left there.
abstract.cn: 想象一把伞被丢在地板上，就那样放着。

abstract.en: Picture a signature trailing off the edge of the page.
abstract.cn: 想象一个签名一路拖到纸边之外。

abstract.en: Picture a door swinging open behind someone who does not look back.
abstract.cn: 想象有人头也不回地走开，身后门大敞着。

examples.en: He carelessly threw the wet umbrella on the floor.
examples.cn: 他把湿伞随手丢在地板上。

examples.en: He carelessly left the gate open all night.
examples.cn: 他粗心地把门开了一整夜。

examples.en: She carelessly waved away the warning.
examples.cn: 她漫不经心地挥挥手，把警告打发掉了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「开尔莱斯利」——心里没关上 care，动作就松散。

root: careless + -ly；care 源自古英语 caru（忧虑、挂念），-less 意为「没有…的」。

sensesIntro.en: One adverb, two tones: a fault that causes errors, and a lightness that shrugs at results.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个副词，两种语气：会造成错误的过失，和满不在乎的轻松。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loose grip that lets something fall.
core.cn: 核心意象：松开的握持，让东西掉了下去。

branches.en: The fault sense: the missing attention produces mistakes.
branches.cn: 过失义：缺失的注意力造成了错误。

branches.en: The casual sense: the missing concern looks like ease.
branches.cn: 随意义：缺失的关切表现为轻松。

branches.en: drive carelessly and carelessly handled are the warning phrases.
branches.cn: 疏忽驾驶与处理草率是常见的警示说法。

branches.en: Both senses come from the same absence, judged by its results.
branches.cn: 两个义项同出一源，只是按结果作出不同评价。

branches.en: speak carelessly can mean speaking without weighing words, not necessarily with harm.
branches.cn: speak carelessly 可指说话不加斟酌，未必造成伤害。

intro.en: Carelessly stacks three pieces: care, -less, and -ly.
intro.cn: carelessly 叠加了三个部件：care、-less、-ly。

latinIntro.en: All parts are native English, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 全部部件都是英语本族语，因此不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: The box was carelessly packed.
items.exampleCN: 这个箱子打包得很草率。

items.example: A careless move broke the seal.
items.exampleCN: 一个疏忽的动作弄坏了封条。

items.meaning: the state of not caring enough
items.example: Carelessness caused the delay.
Handle the box with care.
A careful check found the error.
items.exampleCN: 一次仔细的检查发现了错误。

items.example: She carefully closed the lid.
The holiday felt carefree.
items.exampleCN: 这个假期让人无忧无虑。

items.example: Caru is the oldest form.

definition_en: the goods carried by a ship, aircraft, or large vehicle
core_image: 船舱里堆得满满的木箱
scene: 这艘船装载着一批木材。The ship was carrying a cargo of timber.
sceneCN: 这里 cargo 是「货物」（第 1 个义项：船或飞机运载的一批货）；句意是这艘船装载着一批木材。

derivatives.zh: 语义关联词，义为「货运；货物」，常与 cargo 互换
语义关联词，义为「装运的一批货」
语义关联词，义为「负载；装载量」

senses.title: Goods carried by a ship or aircraft
senses.definition: the goods that a ship, aircraft, or large vehicle carries
senses.definitionCN: 船、飞机或大型车辆所运载的货物
senses.example: The port handles cargo from all over the world.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口处理来自世界各地的货物。
senses.why: Spanish cargo meant a loading or a burden, and English kept that sense of goods loaded aboard.
senses.whyCN: 西班牙语 cargo 意为「装载、负担」，英语保留了「装到船上的货」这一含义。

senses.title: The full load a carrier can take
senses.definition: the total amount of goods that a ship or aircraft is carrying or can carry
senses.definitionCN: 一艘船或一架飞机所载或能载的货物总量
senses.example: The vessel returned with a full cargo of grain.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘船满载谷物返航。
senses.why: If cargo is what is loaded, then a full cargo names the complete load, not just some goods.
senses.whyCN: 既然 cargo 是装上的货，那么 a full cargo 就指完整的载货量，而不只是部分货物。

intro.en: Cargo comes from a Spanish word for loading, and behind it stands the Latin wagon.
intro.cn: cargo 来自西班牙语中表示「装载」的词，背后仍是拉丁语的「车」。

items.en: carrus named a wagon, the base of a whole family of loading words.
items.cn: carrus 指马车，是整组「装载」词汇的基础。

items.en: carricare meant to load a wagon or a cart.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 carricare 意为「往车上装货」。

items.en: cargo named a load or a burden, especially the goods on a ship.
items.cn: 西班牙语 cargo 指负载或负担，尤指船上的货物。

items.en: English borrowed cargo through trade for the goods carried by a vessel.
items.cn: 英语通过贸易借入 cargo，指船只运载的货物。

items.en: The word extended to aircraft and lorries, and to air cargo as a fixed phrase.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到飞机和货车，并形成 air cargo 这样的固定说法。

note.en: Cargo belongs to the Latin wagon family and sits beside freight and shipment.
note.cn: cargo 属于拉丁语「车」词族，同时与 freight、shipment 相邻。

entries.definition: to ask a price, or to load something with a task or duty
entries.definitionCN: 收费，或使承担任务；与 cargo 同出 carricare（装车）。

entries.definition: a vehicle for passengers, or the act of carrying
entries.definitionCN: 载客车厢，或运送行为，与 cargo 同根。

entries.definition: a person or company that transports goods
entries.definitionCN: 运输货物的人或公司，与 cargo 同根。

entries.definition: goods carried by ship, train, or lorry
entries.definitionCN: 由船、火车或卡车运载的货物，常与 cargo 互换。

entries.definition: a load of goods sent together
entries.definitionCN: 一起发运的一批货物。
